record.paper_title: Lower Bounds for Unrestricted Boolean Circuits: Open Problems
record.original_question: Can one prove multiplicative-complexity lower bounds mc(f) ≥ n, or even mc(f) ≥ (1 + ε)n, for explicit Boolean functions f, where mc(f) is the minimum number of AND-type gates needed to compute f when XOR-type gates are treated as free?

evidence.quote: What if some gates are given for free? Basically, each gate in a binary Boolean circuit is either an XOR-type gate ... or an AND-type gate ...
The minimum number of AND-type gates required to compute f is known as multiplicative complexity of f, mc(f).
Strangely enough, this is the strongest known lower bound: we do not know how to prove mc(f) ≥ n, let alone proving mc(f) ≥ (1 + )n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider Boolean circuits over the De Morgan/XOR basis in which each gate is one of two types:
- XOR-type gates: gates computing an affine function over GF(2), such as XOR, NOT, or constants (these are treated as "free");
- AND-type gates: gates computing a non-affine binary function over GF(2), such as AND.

For a Boolean function f : {0,1}^n → {0,1}, define the multiplicative complexity mc(f) to be the minimum number of AND-type gates appearing in any such circuit that computes f (with no restriction on the number of XOR-type gates).

The problem is to exhibit an explicit family of Boolean functions f_n : {0,1}^n → {0,1} (computable, say, in polynomial time, or otherwise given by an explicit construction) for which one can prove the lower bound
    mc(f_n) ≥ n,
and, more ambitiously, to prove a lower bound of the form
    mc(f_n) ≥ (1 + ε) n
for some absolute constant ε > 0 and all sufficiently large n.
artifact.status_search_result: Available literature indicates that the strongest known multiplicative-complexity lower bound for an explicit Boolean function is still essentially n−1 (via the dim(f)/2 bound and similar arguments), and no explicit function is known to satisfy mc(f) ≥ n, let alone mc(f) ≥ (1+ε)n. Recent work focuses on concrete multiplicative complexity of small or symmetric functions and on exact values for low-MC classes, but the asymptotic lower-bound question for explicit functions remains open.

status_evidence.title: Circuit Complexity and Multiplicative Complexity of Boolean Functions (Kulikov)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discusses the dim(f)/2 lower bound on multiplicative complexity and the lack of stronger bounds for explicit functions.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit function is known with mc(f) ≥ n; the best general lower bound techniques yield bounds essentially of order n via dimension arguments.

status_evidence.title: Concrete Multiplicative Complexity of Symmetric Functions (NIST)
status_evidence.snippet: Provides upper and lower bounds on multiplicative complexity of specific symmetric functions; bounds remain at most linear in n.
status_evidence.claim: Known concrete lower bounds on mc for explicit symmetric functions do not exceed linear order, consistent with the (1+ε)n barrier remaining unbroken.

status_evidence.title: Boolean Functions with Multiplicative Complexity 3 and 4
status_evidence.snippet: Classifies Boolean functions of low multiplicative complexity; recent activity is on small-MC classification rather than super-linear explicit lower bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Recent research focuses on small multiplicative complexity classes; no super-(1+ε)n lower bound for explicit functions is reported.
